intro.heading: Install LIMEN
intro.summary: Set up the compiler, build the native modules, and check that HashLink can load them.
requirements.heading: Before you start
requirements.downloads: Install Haxe and run haxe --version in a new terminal. Download or clone the LIMEN source code. If you downloaded a ZIP, extract it and name the directory Limen.
requirements.binaries: Check the LIMEN releases. If a build matches your OS and architecture, extract it and use the prebuilt native modules with the bundled or a compatible version of HashLink. Otherwise, build the modules using the steps below.
requirements.title: Haxe and HashLink
requirements.paragraph: Haxe compiles your code to bytecode, and HashLink runs it. LIMEN works with standard HashLink. For easier installation and updates, HashLink NMB provides hl limen install and hl limen update.
requirements.paragraph2: Required to build LIMEN's native components.
requirements.paragraph3: Used by the build.sh and build.bat scripts.
requirements.paragraph4: Build standard HashLink or HashLink NMB before building LIMEN. By default the script looks for the HashLink source in the sibling ../hashlink-nmb directory. If you keep it elsewhere, pass the path with --hashlink-root.
install.heading: Build the project
install.paragraph: The script fetches dependencies, configures CMake, and writes the binaries to build/bin/<platform>-<configuration>.
check.heading: Verify the installation
check.paragraph: From the LIMEN root, go to the official window example. Before running it, copy limen.hdll into the example directory. If you use the bundled Windows runtime, also copy hl.exe and libhl.dll and use .\hl.exe exwindow.hl as the final command.
check.title: Native module
check.paragraph2: HashLink must be able to find the built limen.hdll at startup. If the module fails to load, check where you placed the binaries and where the loader searches for native libraries.
check.paragraph3: The README notes that macOS CI builds are temporarily disabled. If no prebuilt archive is available, follow the source build instructions.
troubleshooting.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.haxe: If haxe or hl is missing, open a new terminal after installation and check PATH. In PowerShell, run the executable in the current directory with .\hl.exe.
troubleshooting.source: If you get Type not found : limen..., check which directory you're running haxe build.hxml from. In the tutorial projects, -cp .. should point to the LIMEN repository root.
troubleshooting.native: If limen.hdll fails to load, check that it's next to the bytecode and that HashLink and the native modules target the same architecture. On Linux and macOS, also check the dynamic library dependencies.
troubleshooting.gl: If OpenGL is unavailable or context creation fails, use opengl.limen from the same build as limen.hdll and check that your driver supports OpenGL 3.3 for the game example.
